description.narrative: The proposed project aims to enhance the capacity of government agencies for improved public service delivery by expanding accessibility to public services, integrating service delivery systems and decentralising their access.

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative: 1.1 The current regulations related to public service delivery needs to be amended in order to better suit the PSC service delivery modality 1.2 Public services delivery processes should apply new and unified Public Services Standards 1.3 No comprehensive assessments conducted aimed to improving the quality of public services delivery based on analytical tools developed 2.1 Personal of PSA, MoJ and other associated government agencies not trained through developed modules (disaggregated by gender) 2.2 Absence of roadmap documents on transfer of front-office operations from relevant government agencies to PSCs 3.1 No new and innovative Public Cervices Centers in project pilot regions are not established and equipped with relevant IT hardware and software 3.2 Absence of regular awareness raising activities/items, i.e. TV/radio advertisements, printed material, infographics, videos, etc. aimed at broadcasting public services in rural areas 4.1 Absence of dashboard for monitoring activities of PSCs in real time at the MoJ and PSA level 4.2 Absence of institutional arrangements to engage citizens, especially women, in planning local budgets and monitoring their execution in regions

1.1. At least nine (9) regulations amended with the support of the project to better suit the PSC public service delivery modality. Evidence: 1) National Strategy for the Modernization and Accelerated Development of the Public Service Delivery System for 2022–2026, which was approved by the Decree of the President of Uzbekistan ‘On additional measures to simplify the provision of public services, reduce bureaucratic barriers, and develop a national system for the provision of public services’ on 20 April 2022 (http://surl.li/dqbqh). 2) Draft Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan On Public Services was developed and under review by the Ministry of Justice, 3) The recommendations on improving the system of registration of civil status were included into the Resolution No. 540 of the Cabinet of Ministers dd. 28.09.2022 On measures to further improve the procedures for writing civil status documents and draft Decree of the President of the RUz On measures to further improve the system for the provision of public services in the field of registry offices (https://lex.uz/docs/5865484). 4) Recommendations for improving the pension system with a focus to digitalize and introduce proactive services were included into the Decree of the President of the RUz No. PF-74 dd. 17.02.2022 On additional measures to support persons with disabilities and the population in need of social protection (https://lex.uz/docs/5865484), 5) The recommendations for introduction of online notary services were included into the Decree of the President of the RUz No. PF-89 dd. 17.03.2022 “On measures to further increase the effectiveness of justice bodies and institutions in ensuring the rights and freedoms of citizens and providing legal services” (https://lex.uz/docs/5914998), 6) Draft of the Communication Strategy and Road for promoting public services of the Republic of Uzbekistan for 2023–2026 is developed and under consideration by the Ministry of Justice, 6) The draft of Decree of President of Uzbekistan “On measures to further accelerate the wide involvement of the private sector in the processes of implementation of state functions and services” at the stage of approval by the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan. 7) The draft Quality Assessment Methodology of PSD developed and under approval by the Ministry of Justice. 8) Inputs provided to the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers No. 200 of 20.04.2022 “On approval of single administrative building regulations in the field of construction” (https://lex.uz/ru/docs/5971316). 9) Recommendations provided for the Resolution of the Cabinet of Ministers No. 169 of 11 April 2022 “On measures to further support volunteerism” (https://lex.uz/en/docs/5953755).
1.2. Six (6) Public Service Standards are developed. Evidence: - Six new national standards in the area of delivering the general organizational and technical rules of e-public services were developed and introduced (http://surl.li/dryqe). - The central office of the Public Services Agency, five pilot regional departments and five pilot Public Services Centers received certificates of compliance for the ISO quality management system 9001:2015.
1.3. 10 proposals on improving quality of public service delivery based on analytical tools developed to assess quality levels of service delivery. Evidence: - Functional Review and Business Process Re-engineering of the Cadastre Agency under the State Tax Committee of the Republic of Uzbekistan - http://surl.li/drxvo. - Functional Review and Business Process Reengineering of the Ministry of construction of the Republic of Uzbekistan - http://surl.li/drxwa.
2.1. 2000 personnel (of which at least 400 women) PSA, MoJ and other associated government agencies personnel trained through developed modules (disaggregated by gender) trained? Evidence: 12 training modules were developed on different topics identified as per the needs assessment (leadership, result based management, HR management, strategic planning, stress management and etc.). In total, 2000 personnel (of which at least 400 women) from MoJ, back offices, local khokimiyats and Public Relations (PR) and outreach specialists of front and back offices trained through developed modules (disaggregated by gender) trained. Link to related data: https://u.to/cwL1Gw and links to some training modules: https://u.to/1Qr1Gw and https://u.to/GAz1Gw.
2.2. 1 roadmap document developed on transfer of front-office operations from relevant government agencies to PSCs Evidence: A National Strategy for Modernization and Accelerated Development of Public Services for 2022-2026 and its implementation Roadmap developed and approved by the Decree of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan dated 20 April 2022 PF-113 ‘On additional measures to simplify the provision of public services, reduce bureaucratic barriers and develop the national system of public services’ - http://surl.li/drxwr.
2.3. 6 new PSCs established using ergonomic principles and are equipped with the appropriate IT hardware and software from the start of the project. Evidence: The project has already provided practical support to the PSA in the creation of 6 pilot Public Services Centers (Nurafshan city, Bakhmal, Khavast, Dekhkanabad, Shurchi, Yangi Namangan) and 2 additional PSCs in Bandigon and Khujaily districts. PSC in Yangi Namangan district of Namangan region was started operation in March 2022. One more PSC is planned to be opened in Nukus district of the Republic of Karakalpakstan as soon as the construction works will be finalized. These centers are equipped with the IT equipment, furniture, children’s playgrounds. During the establishment of each center a special attention was paid to the creation of favorable conditions for all categories of the population, including people with the disabilities, that ensured the inclusiveness of pilot public services centers. Volunteers were trained andstarted to support the PSA/PSCs staff in pilot centers, 7 women advisory groups (WAGs) are fully operating that were established last year with the close cooperation of the NGO Marta (Latvia) started to provide advisory support the rural population. Links to news: http://surl.li/drydg; http://surl.li/drydl, https://u.to/axD1Gw; https://u.to/3xL1Gw; https://u.to/6xL1Gw
3.2. In total, more than 50 awareness-raising items, i.e. TV/radio advertisements, printed material, infographics, videos, etc. developed and published. Evidence: More than 300 posts were prepared and posted on various social networks and more than 130 news and analytical articles were published in local and national media, 5 blogs and 6 article were published in international media, while 18 thematic infographics, 1 cartoon and 5 animated videos were developed for display at all PSCs, 12 videos on improving public services and how to get them. Dozens of interviews and news stories were broadcast on local and national TV channels. The ‘Tez, oson, qulay’ Facebook page was created to inform the population about public services and how to obtain them, changes in public service delivery, and to share new ideas and initiatives – the page had about 3,000 subscribers. More than 4 million potential beneficiaries across the country have been informed about the activities of the PSA and PSCs, and the public assistance available at the unified portal of public services www.my.gov.uz and the website davxizmat.uz.
4.1. Dashboard for monitoring activities of PSCs in real time at the MoJ and PSA level is developed and available. Evidence: A new Situation centre was established and online tool for monitoring the activity of all PSCs across the country introduced at the Ministry of Justice. It also allows analysis of data obtained through different information systems in public service delivery. A set of data storage servers and equipment for situational center in Tashkent were procured and installed. CKICK-Sense software was procured and being installed as an online tool. All 207 PSCs are connected to situational center for real time integrated monitoring system, including visual monitoring through installed cameras in each PSC.
4.2. Institutional arrangements are partially established and are available to engage citizens, especially women, in planning local budgets and monitoring their execution in regions. Evidence: - 7 Women Advisory Groups were established in 7 pilot district PSCs, more than 5,400 consultations delivered to women and other people with special needs, on matters related to public services, mental health and social subjects. - 6 Public Advisory Councils were established under local khokimiyats and more than 12 decisions of local khokimiyats including local budgets and monitoring their execution were developed by engagement of citizens.

1.1. Two (2) regulation amended with the support of the project to better suit the PSC public service delivery modality. Evidence: 1) The project has contributed to the development of the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan “On Licensing, Permitting and Notification Procedures” (No. ZRU-701 dated 14.07.2021), which also made it possible to digitalize the entire licensing system by introducing a new “License” information system and enabling entrepreneurs to obtain 31 licenses, permits and notifications. Link: https://license.gov.uz/ 2) As a result of the analytical work assessing the current situation in Uzbekistan, as well as the benchmarking of international good practices, a National Public Service Delivery System Development Strategy for 2022-2026 and Round Map was developed as the cornerstone of “citizen-centric” public services. Currently, the document in the format of the draft of the Presidential Decree was sent by the Ministry of Justice to the Cabinet of Ministers and the President’s Administration for consideration. Link: https://u.to/UAL1Gw
1.3. Three proposals for improving the quality of public services delivery based on analytical tools developed to assess quality levels of service delivery Evidence. 1) set of recommendations and advice to improve mobile service delivery process were shared with PSA based on joint assessment of IPSD & Acceleration Laboratory in two pilot regions (Jizzakh and Syrdarya regions). Report is available here: https://u.to/vQH1Gw. 2) a number of practical recommendations to improve of 2 public services’ regulations related to the nostrification were shared with PSA based on BPR report which conducted in three pilot regions. Link: https://u.to/EQL1Gw 3) set of practical recommendations, advises and guidance to improve 10 most demanded public services’ regulations were shared with PSA based on quality assessment report conducted in five pilot regions. Link: Quality assessment of public service delivery report. Link: https://u.to/IwL1Gw
2.1. 800 (including 245 women) from PSA, MoJ and other associated government agencies personnel trained through developed modules and capacity building exercises. Evidence: 10 training modules were developed on Leadership, Result based management, HR management, Strategic planning, Stress management and etc.). In total, during the year more than 30 different trainings and capacity building exercises organized by the project and participated by about 800 specialists (245 women) from the front and back offices of public services and regional and district administrations. Link to related data: https://u.to/cwL1Gw and links to some training modules: https://u.to/1Qr1Gw and https://u.to/GAz1Gw
3.1. Seven (7) PSC established using ergonomic principles equipped with relevant IT hardware and software Evidence: The project has already provided practical support to the PSA in the creation of 7 Public Services Centers (Nurafshan city, Bakhmal, Khavast, Dekhkanabad, Shurchi, Bandigon and Khujaily districts). These centers are equipped with the IT equipment, furniture, children’s playgrounds. During the establishment of each center a special attention was paid to the creation of favorable conditions for all categories of the population, including people with the disabilities, that ensured the inclusiveness of pilot public services centers. Volunteers were trained and started to support the PSA/PSCs staff in pilot centers, 7 women advisory groups (WAGs) are fully operating that were established last year with the close cooperation of the NGO Marta (Latvia) started to provide advisory support the rural population. Links to news: https://u.to/qRL1Gw; https://u.to/axD1Gw; https://u.to/3xL1Gw; https://u.to/6xL1Gw
3.2. Four (4) groups (30 pcs.) awareness raising items, i.e. TV/radio advertisements, printed material, infographics, videos, etc. Evidence: - 6 infographics were prepared on the new 6 standards of public services. Link: https://u.to/ggL1Gw - 4 posters developed and disseminated: (1) How to receive public services; (2) How to get STIR; (3) The process of online queuing; (4) Public service inventory algorithm. Link: https://u.to/jQL1Gw - special project’s page in the Facebook created and more than 1000 subscribers (Link: https://u.to/ExP1Gw. - 18 TV/radio materials were developed within awareness raising activities. Link: https://u.to/mQL1Gw
4.1 Dashboard for monitoring activities of PSCs in real time at the MoJ and PSA level is partially developed and available. Evidence. The Project provided the Situational Center with IT equipment (computers, monitors, servers, etc.) and a special “Qlick Sense” software for Business Intelligence system. ToR for the Unified Platform of the PSA is developed, and “Qlick Sense” software will be integrated into the new developed Unified platform Link: https://u.to/3Ab1Gw
4.2. Institutional arrangements are partially established and are available to engage citizens, especially women, in planning local budgets and monitoring their execution in regions. Evidence. • 7 Woman advisory groups established under PSC in 7 pilot districts with the help of MARTA Center (Latvia) and Civic initiatives support center, NGO (Uzbekistan). WAGs helped 5362 women and vulnerable people to obtain public services both at Public Service Centers and online through the my.gov.uz website, offered legal and psychological consultations, organized trainings. Link: https://u.to/oQL1Gw • 3 Public advisory councils established under the khokimiyats and Kengashes of people’s deputies in 3 pilot districts (Shurchi, Khavast and Kasansay districts). Link: https://u.to/qgL1Gw New reporting system was introduced in 2 pilot district khokimiyats (Dekhkanabad and Kasansay districts) using Key Performance Indicators (KPI). Link: https://u.to/qgL1Gw • Draft Law on Local government in new edition was prepared and submitted to the Ministry of Justice. It is suggested to separate the position of Khokim (Head of executive authority) from position of Head of Kengashes of people’s deputies (Head of representative authority), wide engagement of citizens, especially women, in planning local budgets and monitoring their execution. Link: https://clck.ru/V5P29 • Since January 2021 new Secretariats of Kengashes of people’s deputies in all districts of Uzbekistan established. Within joint plan of the Senate of the Oliy Majlis and IPSD it was prepared and approved by the Senate’s Resolution a Regulation for newly established Secretariats and Regulations for Kengashes’ Commissions. Link: https://u.to/HhP1Gw.
